newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo gold futures firmer in lacklustre trade.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo gold futures firmer in lacklustre trade.

text.p: Yen-denominated gold futures ended slightly firmer on Friday in lacklustre and rangebound trade, moving in line with the currency market, traders said.

Japanese traders were focusing the International Monetary Fund's (IMF) board meeting to discuss gold sales on Friday, but traders said further falls could be limited in the short term as the plan has been mostly discounted in current prices.
Gold prices ranged from two to seven yen per gram firmer. Most active benchmark August was five yen firmer at 1,342 yen.
Spot gold was quoted at $382.20/50 per ounce at the Tokyo close, against $382.45/382.95 in New York on Thursday.
The gold market largely ignored rising Middle East tensions, the traders said.
In the spot gold market, selling by overseas investors was detected during Asian hours, but otherwise the market was quiet.
Platinum futures ended weaker as weaker spot platinum prices stimulated selling by Japanese trade houses.

"Sentiment in the platinum market is bearish. Amid a lack of buying interest in platinum futures by private investors, spot platinum is vulnerable to the further downside risk, a trading house trader said.

Traders said recent static futures prices and a lack of buying incentives had thinned trading volume of platinum futures. They said Japan's platinum demand had been lacklustre due to a fragile economic recovery at home.
Silver and palladium futures were narrowly mixed in sluggish trade. Silver ranged from 3.0 yen per 10 grams lower to 0.6 yen firmer. Benchmark August was up 0.2 yen at 181.3.

Palladium futures ranged from six yen per gram weaker to two firmer. Benchmark August palladium was two yen firmer at 435 yen. Japanese financial markets will be closed on Monday for a national holiday.
